Zo koppelt: Waarom dit belangrijk Veel o: How to connect: Why this matters: Many entrepreneurs lose time to manual bank and payment transactions or only discover errors at month-end closing. The result: an unclear cash position, delays in accounts receivable management and additional costs for your administration. This step-by-step plan helps you to connect payment data to your accounting securely and in a verifiable way, so you can make the right decisions faster.
Wat is het signaal en wat betekent het v: What is the signal and what does it mean for your company? Signal: you notice that payments do not appear automatically in the accounting, or that many transactions must be processed manually. Context: this often happens because payment platforms (card terminals/pin, webshops, payment apps) and your accounting software do not have a direct or well-configured data flow. Consequence: extra working hours, errors during matching and reduced visibility of available liquidity.
Kun ik mijn betaalapp rechtstreeks koppe: Can I connect my payment app directly to my accounting? Practical answer: sometimes yes, sometimes no — it depends on two things: 1) whether your payment party (bank, POS, PSP) can provide data via an API or webhooks and 2) whether your accounting software accepts that connection. An important technical building block is OAuth 2.0: Twinfield, for example, uses OAuth 2.0 for API access (app registers client-ID, user gives consent and an access token is issued). That means that if your payment provider and your accounting package both support API access and a consent flow, a direct connection is technically possible, but there is often development work or an intermediary layer required.
Praktisch stappenplan: van signaal naar: Practical step-by-step plan: from signal to lasting improvement 1) Inventory (owner: entrepreneur or financial responsible) - Collect the signal: how often do differences occur? Note examples of missed or incorrect transactions from the past month. - Document systems: payment options (card terminals/pin, webshop, payment link, acquirer), bank, accounting software, POS/cash register system. - End result: clear overview of systems and three concrete example transactions.
Handige controlevragen voor uw boekhoude: Useful control questions for your accountant or technical supplier - Does our accounting package support an automatic bank feed or API connection? (If the package is Twinfield: ask about OAuth 2.0 registration and access flow.) - Can the payment party send webhooks or offer API endpoints with transaction data? - Which fields do you use to automatically match payments to invoices? - How are partial payments, chargebacks and refunds handled? - What test data do we need to safely validate the connection?
Praktische werkbare meetpunten en verant: Practical workable metrics and responsibilities (example) - Decision: we hire a developer for a webhook integration. Owner: financial manager. - Action: developer builds integration, bookkeeper validates mapping in a test environment. Time horizon: 6 weeks (prepare, build, test, roll out). - Result metric: within 4 weeks after go-live at least 90% of payments automatically matched (target value as a starting point; set your own standard). - Learnings: after 8 weeks analyze the discrepant transactions and adjust rules.
